examples.en: My clothes got soaked in the sudden rain.
The news was so sudden that I was shocked.
The appointment was suddenly canceled.
It was hard to adapt to the abrupt change.

examples.ko: 할아버지의 급작스러운 입원에 가족이 모두 모였어요.
examples.en: The whole family gathered after Grandpa's sudden hospitalization.
It was sudden, but we handled it well.

explain: '갑작스럽다'와 거의 같게 쓰는데, 말할 때는 '갑작스럽다'가 훨씬 흔해요. ㅂ 불규칙이라 '급작스러워요', '급작스러운'으로 바뀌어요. 주로 '급작스러운 변화'처럼 명사 앞에서 써요.
explain_en: Used almost like 갑작스럽다, which is much more common in speech. It is a ㅂ-irregular, so it becomes 급작스러워요 and 급작스러운. It mostly appears before a noun, as in '급작스러운 변화'.

examples.en: Where are you going on vacation this summer?
The beaches are really crowded in the holiday season.

examples.ko: 우리 가족은 매년 제주도로 바캉스를 가요.
examples.en: My family goes to Jeju Island on vacation every year.
I feel much better after coming back from my vacation.

examples.ko: 회사 동료들이 바캉스 계획을 이야기하고 있어요.
examples.en: My coworkers are talking about their vacation plans.

examples.ko: 짐을 쌀 때 바캉스에 꼭 필요한 것부터 챙겼어요.
examples.en: When I packed, I first gathered what I really needed for the trip.

explain: '바캉스'는 주로 여름에 바다나 휴양지로 떠나는 여행 같은 휴가에 어울려요. 회사에서 쉬는 날이나 휴가 제도를 말할 때는 '휴가'를 써요. '바캉스를 가다', '바캉스 철'처럼 자주 말해요.
explain_en: 바캉스 suggests a trip to the sea or a resort, usually in summer. For days off from work or the leave system, use 휴가. Common phrases are 바캉스를 가다 and 바캉스 철.

examples.en: The situation in the match was reversed in the last five minutes.
The mood suddenly turned around, and everyone was surprised.

examples.ko: 사진의 좌우가 반전돼서 글자가 거꾸로 보여요.
examples.en: The photo is flipped left to right, so the letters look backward.
Everyone was surprised at the result in which the ranking was reversed.
The crowd cheered the moment the situation turned around.
I did not know the story would turn out like this.

explain: 명사 '반전'은 '반전 영화', '반전이 있다'처럼 이야기가 예상과 반대로 바뀔 때 써요. 능동은 '반전시키다'예요. 사진이나 화면이 좌우로 뒤집힐 때도 써요.
explain_en: The noun '반전' is used for a twist, as in '반전 영화' (twist movie) and '반전이 있다' (there is a twist). The active form is '반전시키다'. It also describes a photo or screen being flipped left to right.

examples.ko: 아이가 화가 나서 문을 향해 발길질을 했어요.
examples.en: The child got angry and kicked at the door.
I kicked hard at the ball.

examples.ko: 자는 동안 발길질이 심해서 이불이 다 벗겨졌어요.
examples.en: I kicked a lot in my sleep, so the blanket came all the way off.
The puppy flails its hind legs as if kicking.

examples.ko: 아기가 기저귀를 갈 때 계속 발길질해요.
examples.en: The baby keeps kicking while I change the diaper.
You shouldn't kick around carelessly just because you're angry.

explain: '발로 차다'보다 반복되거나 거친 느낌이 있어요. 아기가 버둥거리거나 화가 나서 마구 차는 장면에 어울려요. 손으로 치는 건 '주먹질'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It feels more repeated or rough than '발로 차다'. It fits a baby flailing or someone kicking wildly out of anger. Hitting with fists is called '주먹질'.

examples.en: The fishy smell fills the room.
I added ginger to get rid of the fishy smell.

examples.ko: 손에서 비린내가 나서 여러 번 씻었어요.
examples.en: My hands smelled fishy, so I washed them several times.

examples.ko: 이 생선은 비린내가 전혀 안 나요.
examples.en: This fish has no fishy smell at all.
As I entered the market, a fishy smell hit me.
If you sprinkle lemon juice, the fishy smell lessens.

explain: '비린내가 나다/풍기다', '비린내를 없애다/잡다'로 써요. 생선이나 날것에서 나는 냄새예요. 고기 쪽 냄새는 '누린내'라고 해요.
explain_en: You say '비린내가 나다/풍기다' and '비린내를 없애다/잡다'. It is the smell from fish or raw food. The smell of meat is called '누린내'.

examples.en: This weekend our club is going on an overnight trip.
At the trip, we played games and talked all night.
We chose a pension in Gangwon-do for the trip.

examples.ko: 신입생 엠티에 가면 친구를 빨리 사귈 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you go on the freshman trip, you can make friends quickly.

examples.ko: 엠티 때 입을 편한 옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed comfortable clothes to wear on the trip.

examples.ko: 엠티가 끝나고 집에 오니 너무 피곤했어요.
examples.en: When I got home after the trip, I was exhausted.

explain: 대학교 동아리, 학과, 회사 사람들이 함께 1박 이상 놀러 가는 모임을 말해요. 보통 '엠티를 가다'라고 해요. 한국에서 만든 줄임말이라 영어권에서는 이 뜻으로 잘 통하지 않아요.
explain_en: It means a gathering where members of a university club, department or company travel together for at least one night. People usually say '엠티를 가다'. It is an abbreviation made in Korea, so it is not understood in this sense in English-speaking countries.

examples.en: The ceremony starts at twelve.
I went to my friend's wedding ceremony.

examples.ko: 예식 때 주차장이 가득 차서 오래 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The parking lot was full during the ceremony, so I waited a long time.
We had a small ceremony with family only.

examples.ko: 예식이 끝나고 다 같이 밥을 먹었어요.
examples.en: After the ceremony, we all ate together.
We set the ceremony date for autumn.

explain: 주로 결혼식을 가리키지만 원래는 정해진 격식을 갖춘 행사 전체를 말해요. 일상에서는 '결혼식'이라고 하고, '예식'은 '예식장'(결혼식장)처럼 합쳐서 많이 써요. 장례는 '장례식'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It most often points to a wedding but originally covers any formal event done by set protocol. In daily speech people say 결혼식; 예식 is common in compounds like 예식장 (wedding hall). A funeral is called 장례식.

examples.en: Many disaster victims lost their homes to the flood.
Disaster victims are staying in the school gymnasium.

examples.ko: 우리 반은 이재민을 돕기 위해 모금을 했어요.
examples.en: Our class raised money to help disaster victims.
Blankets and food were delivered to the wildfire victims.

examples.ko: 뉴스는 이재민 수가 천 명이 넘는다고 전했어요.
examples.en: The news said the number of disaster victims exceeds a thousand.
Volunteers made lunch boxes for the disaster victims.

explain: 홍수, 산불, 지진 같은 재해로 집과 생활을 잃은 사람이에요. 뉴스에서 '이재민 돕기', '이재민이 발생하다'처럼 나와요. 전쟁이나 박해 때문에 나라를 떠난 사람은 '난민'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It covers people who lost their homes and daily life to disasters like floods, wildfires, and earthquakes. News uses 이재민 돕기 and 이재민이 발생하다. People who left their country because of war or persecution are 난민.

examples.en: A large company announced the takeover of a small firm.
The takeover price was too high, so I gave up.

examples.ko: 그 회사의 인수로 직원 수가 늘었어요.
examples.en: The number of employees grew after that company's takeover.
Please sign the receipt confirmation for the baggage.
When the takeover is done, the name will change.
The two companies agreed to the takeover.

explain: '회사 인수'처럼 회사를 사서 넘겨받을 때 써요. 회사를 파는 쪽이 넘기는 일은 '매각'이라고 해요. '인수합병'은 회사를 사고 합치는 일이에요.
explain_en: It is used for buying a company and taking it over, as in '회사 인수'. When the seller hands a company over, that is called '매각'. '인수합병' means buying companies and merging them.

examples.en: The Wi-Fi suddenly won't connect.
You get a notification when you are connected to the server.
I liked that the site connected right away.
It's hard to get connected now because there are many users.
I got connected to the meeting, but there's no sound.
Please check the devices that are connected.

explain: 사람이 하는 행동은 '접속하다', 연결이 되었거나 안 된 상태는 '접속되다'라고 해요. 그래서 '접속이 안 돼요', '접속이 안 되네요'처럼 인터넷이 안 될 때 아주 자주 들어요. '연결되다'는 전화나 사람 사이에도 쓰지만 '접속되다'는 주로 인터넷·서버에 써요.
explain_en: What a person does is 접속하다; the state of being connected or failing to connect is 접속되다. You hear '접속이 안 돼요' all the time when the internet fails. 연결되다 also covers phones and relationships, but 접속되다 is mostly for the internet and servers.

examples.en: Because of heavy rain, they suspend the construction.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 약을 당분간 중지하라고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor told me to stop the medicine for a while.
I will pause exercising from tomorrow.
Please explain the reason for stopping first.

examples.ko: 서비스를 중지하고 나서 사과 글을 올렸어요.
examples.en: After suspending the service, they posted an apology.
They halted the match because it was dangerous.

explain: 하던 일을 중간에 멈출 때 써요. '멈추다'는 움직임이나 소리가 서는 일이고, '그만두다'는 아예 끝내는 일이에요. '중지하다'는 공사나 서비스처럼 정해진 일을 멈추고 나중에 다시 할 수 있을 때도 써요.
explain_en: Used when you stop something partway. '멈추다' is for motion or sound coming to a halt, and '그만두다' means quitting for good. '중지하다' fits planned work such as construction or a service that is halted and may resume later.

examples.en: The parcel box arrived crushed.
The car door got dented, so I took it in for repair.
I stepped on the can and it got squashed flat.
A dented pot is inconvenient to use.

examples.ko: 가방 안에서 도시락이 찌그러지지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that the lunchbox doesn't get squashed in your bag.

examples.ko: 공이 찌그러져 있어서 잘 안 굴러가요.
examples.en: The ball is dented, so it doesn't roll well.

explain: 단단한 물건이 눌리거나 부딪혀서 모양이 비뚤어졌을 때 써요. 종이나 옷처럼 부드러운 것이 접히면 '구겨지다'라고 해요. 눌리기 전의 원래 모양이 있다는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: Use it when a firm object loses its shape because it was pressed or hit. For soft things like paper or clothes that get folded, say '구겨지다' instead. It suggests the thing had a proper shape before it was pressed.

examples.ko: 한가위에는 온 가족이 모여 송편을 빚어요.
examples.en: At Hangawi, the whole family gathers to shape songpyeon.

examples.ko: 올해 한가위 보름달이 정말 크고 밝았어요.
examples.en: This year's Hangawi full moon was really big and bright.
It would be wonderful if every day were like Hangawi.
I'm going down to my hometown over the Hangawi holiday.
It's nice to greet people with "Have a bountiful Hangawi."
When Hangawi gets close, the market gets very crowded.

explain: '한가위'는 '추석'의 순우리말이에요. 일상에서는 '추석'이 훨씬 많이 쓰이고, '한가위'는 인사말, 노래, 옛이야기에서 자주 들려요. 음력 8월 15일이에요.
explain_en: '한가위' is the native Korean word for '추석'. In daily talk '추석' is used far more, while '한가위' shows up in greetings, songs, and old sayings. It falls on the 15th day of the 8th lunar month.

examples.ko: 독감 환자 급증 소식에 학교가 휴교하기로 했어요.
examples.en: After news of a sharp rise in flu cases, the school decided to close.

examples.ko: 태풍 때문에 내일 모든 학교가 휴교해요.
examples.en: Because of the typhoon, all schools are closed tomorrow.
I got the news of the school closure by text in the morning.

examples.ko: 눈이 너무 많이 와서 휴교한 학교가 많았어요.
examples.en: It snowed so much that many schools closed.

examples.ko: 학교가 휴교하면 아이들을 돌볼 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: When a school closes, someone is needed to look after the children.
During the school closure, I took classes online.

explain: 학교 전체가 임시로 문을 닫는 것이에요. 한 과목 수업만 쉬는 '휴강'과 달리, 학교 전체가 쉬는 거예요. 방학과 달리 태풍이나 전염병 같은 일 때문에 갑자기 생기는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It is when a whole school temporarily closes. Unlike '휴강', where only one class is skipped, the entire school is off. Unlike a vacation, it often comes suddenly because of things like a typhoon or an epidemic.
